t: Bulgaria surrenders to Byzantine Empire
c: In 1018 Bulgaria surrendered and became part of the Byzantine Empire thus restoring the Danube frontier, which had not been held since the days of Heraclius.

t: Basil II issues law against Dynatoi
c: In 996, Basil II issued a law targeting Dynatoi landowners, demanding restitution of lands acquired illegally and requiring proof of title.

t: Severe drought strikes Black Sea region
c: From 1300 to 1302, a severe drought occurred in the areas surrounding the Black Sea.

c: In the spring of 1241, German, Polish and Hungarian forces were defeated by the Mongols at Legnica and Mohi.

c: When Güyük called Batu to pay him homage several times, Batu sent Yaroslav II, Andrey and Alexander Nevsky to Karakorum in Mongolia in 1247.

t: Alexander installed as grand prince of Vladimir
c: Thanks to his friendship with Sartaq Khan, Batu's son, who was a Christian, Alexander was installed as the grand prince of Vladimir by Batu in 1252.

t: Sartaq Khan appointed after Batu's death
c: After Batu died in 1256, his son Sartaq Khan was appointed by Möngke Khan.

t: Berke enthroned as Khan of Golden Horde
c: Berke, who had been converted to Islam, was enthroned as khan of the Golden Horde in 1257 or 1258.

t: Daniel of Galicia defies Mongols in Podolia
c: In 1256, Daniel of Galicia openly defied the Mongols and ousted their troops in northern Podolia.

t: Mongol census conducted across Russian principalities
c: The Mongol Khan's authority extended to all principalities, and in 1274–1275 the census took place in all cities, including Smolensk and Vitebsk.

t: Töde Möngke succeeds Mengu-Timur as Khan
c: Mengu-Timur was succeeded in 1281 by his brother Töde Möngke, who was a Muslim.

t: Nogai blockades Drăstăr; executes Ivailo
c: He blockaded Michael Asen II inside Drăstăr in 1279 and executed the rebel emperor Ivailo in 1280.

t: Stefan Milutin accepts Mongol supremacy to Nogai
c: Nogai compelled Serbian king Stefan Milutin to accept Mongol supremacy and received his son, Stefan Dečanski, as hostage in 1287.

t: Talabuga and Nogai invade Hungary
c: In 1285, Talabuga and Nogai invaded Hungary.

t: Talabuga plunders Kingdom of Ruthenia
c: In 1287, Talabuga successfully plundered the Kingdom of Ruthenia, especially the region of Volodymyr.

t: Talabuga and Nogai defeated in Poland
c: In late 1287–1288, Talabuga and Nogai attacked Poland but were both defeated.

t: Nogai's invasion of Ilkhanate fails
c: Nogai's army made an unsuccessful attempt to invade the Ilkhanate in 1290.

t: Toqta kills Nogai at Kagamlik
c: Within two years, Toqta returned and killed Nogai in 1299 at the Kagamlik, near the Dnieper.

t: Toqta establishes peace with Ilkhan Gaykhatu
c: Toqta dispatched a peace mission to the Ilkhan Gaykhatu in 1294, and peace was maintained mostly uninterrupted until 1318.

t: Mongol rulers announce general peace proposal
c: In 1304, ambassadors from the Mongol rulers of Central Asia and the Yuan dynasty announced to Toqta their general peace proposal.

t: Jochid princess Tulunbay marries Al-Nasir Muhammad
c: In 1320, the Jochid princess Tulunbay was married to Al-Nasir Muhammad, Sultan of Egypt.

c: The Golden Horde invaded the Ilkhanate under Abu Sa'id in 1318, 1324, and 1335.

t: Ilkhanate and Mamluk Sultan sign peace treaty
c: Öz Beg's ally Al-Nasir refused to attack Abu Sa'id because the Ilkhan and the Mamluk Sultan signed a peace treaty in 1323.

c: Öz Beg's eldest son Tini Beg reigned briefly from 1341 to 1342 before his younger brother, Jani Beg, came to power.

t: Jani Beg fails to seize Caffa
c: In 1344, Jani Beg tried to seize Caffa from the Genoese but failed.

t: Casimir III submits to Golden Horde
c: The Polish king, Casimir III the Great, submitted to the Horde in 1357 and paid tribute in order to avoid more conflicts.

t: Jani Beg conquers Tabriz from Chobanids
c: Jani Beg asserted Jochid dominance over the Chagatai Khanate and conquered Tabriz, ending Chobanid rule there in 1356.

t: Qulpa kills Berdi Beg in coup
c: Berdi Beg was killed in a coup by his brother Qulpa in 1359.

c: Abdullah died in 1370 and Muhammad Bolaq was enthroned as puppet khan by Mamai.

t: Timur attacks Urus Khan indecisively
c: Timur personally attacked Urus in 1376 but the campaign ended indecisively.

t: Tokhtamysh attacks Timur on Syr Darya
c: Tokhtamysh attacked Timur on the Syr Darya in 1389 with a massive army including Russians, Bulgars, Circassians, and Alans.

t: Timur defeats Tokhtamysh at Kondurcha River
c: In 1391, Timur gathered an army 200,000 strong and defeated Tokhtamysh at the Battle of the Kondurcha River.

t: Tokhtamysh ravages Shirvan region
c: Tokhtamysh returned in 1394, ravaging the region of Shirvan.

t: Shadi Beg elected Golden Horde khan
c: Temür Qutlugh died in 1400 and his cousin Shadi Beg was elected khan with Edigu's approval.

t: Temur Khan becomes Golden Horde khan
c: Shadi Beg was replaced by Pulad, who died in 1410 and was succeeded by Temur Khan, the son of Temür Qutlugh.

t: Temur Khan expels Edigu to Khwarezm
c:
Temur Khan turned against Edigu and forced him to flee to Khwarezm in 1411.

c: In 1414, Shah Rukh of the Timurids conquered Khwarezm.

t: Taibuga founds Sibir Khanate dynasty
c: The Khanate of Sibir was ruled by a dynasty originating with Taibuga in 1405 at Chimgi-Tura.

t: Abu'l-Khayr Khan rules Golden Horde
c: After his death in 1428, the khanate was ruled by Abu'l-Khayr Khan.

t: Barak Khan assassinated after defeating invasion
c: Barak defeated an invasion by Ulugh Beg in 1427 but was assassinated the next year.

t: Ulugh Muhammad aids Vytautas against Pskov
c: In 1426, Ulugh Muhammad contributed troops to Vytautas' war against Pskov.
